author: Sameer Alssayyad
attribution: Photo: Sameer Alssayyad, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alkhair_Mosque_-_panoramio.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Sana'a street corner by the Alkhair mosque; target is the small brown vertical honey-and-dates shop sign at the right corner of the building (far, hazy). Distractors: the blue travel-agency banner 'وكالة ...لان للسفريات والسياحة وخدمات الحج والعمرة' (agency name partly unclear), a red honey-shop sign at left and a 'دار ...' sign at far right. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chai,_Hodaidah_Market_(14279955332).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Back-lit coffee-and-spice shop sign at night in the Hodeidah market, with teapot and coffee-cup images. The very large word between 'ياسر' and 'والبهارات' is a stylised form of بن (coffee) with an extra leading stroke; its exact letters (بن / لبن / للبن) cannot be determined reliably, so it is NOT transcribed. Bottom line is partly crossed by a wire (المكسرات obscured but readable). The lower red sign repeats '...ن والبهارات والمكسرات' and is a distractor.

author: Rod Waddington
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/64607715@N05/30351652674. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: li-bay' jami' anwa' al-hinna' wal-luban (for sale of all kinds of henna and frankincense)

notes: Hand-lettered awning valance on a henna shop in Sana'a; the text follows the scalloped edge. 'جملة وتجزئة' is small at the far left; a tiny painter's signature above 'العمري' and a phone number at the left end are not transcribed. The pink sign above the awning and the banner below the counter are distractors.

author: Rod Waddington
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/64607715@N05/46743289222. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hanging black spice-shop board in the old souq of Sana'a, black-and-white photo, seen at an angle with a wire across the top line. Only the clearly legible lines are transcribed; the smaller item labels below (apparently أعشاب طبيه, زيوت طبيه, قهوة ولاد) and a cut-off bottom line are too small to be certain. Distractors: the 'محل أحسن الخلقي' board at left, the awning 'زبيري للعطارة', and a large banner at top right.

author: Rod Waddington
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/64607715@N05/9729046957. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: al-Mu'assasa al-'Amma lil-Ittisalat as-Silkiyya (Public Telecommunication Corporation)

notes: Rooftop board of the Public Telecommunication Corporation, Al-Mahwit branch, shot from below at dusk and partly hidden. Only the visible parts are transcribed: the next Arabic word ('واللا...', i.e. واللاسلكية) and 'PUBL' of PUBLIC are hidden behind the oval 'YemenNet' lightbox, and 'ON' of CORPORATION plus the start of 'المؤسسة' are behind flowering bushes. Small, faint header lines ('Republic of Yemen / Ministry of Telecommunication & Information Technology' at left, Arabic equivalent at right) and the 'YT' logo are not transcribed.

author: Rod Waddington
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/64607715@N05/14613590613. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hand-painted, weathered shop sign above blue shutter doors (women's tailoring/abaya shop), with paintings of veiled women. 'مركز' in white, 'العماد' in stylised gold calligraphy with small decorative marks omitted. Smaller painted lines are only partly legible and not transcribed: left block apparently 'للخياطة وجميع أنواع الأزياء النسائية', right block ending '... العبايات الخليجية', bottom-left owner line 'لصاحبه / ... عماد ...'.

author: Rod Waddington
attribution: Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/64607715@N05/10513389785. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Shop name painted across closed metal shutter doors. In the Latin line 'AL' sits in a small circle and the 'S' is the big white letter of the blue round logo, followed by 'UMOOD EXHIBITION' on a brown band (a latch partly covers one O). Not transcribed: the small white Arabic slogan arcing around the logo, and the large bottom Arabic line (begins 'للت', ends '...يات'), whose middle letters are covered by red spray graffiti.
